minutes.headline: Assessors created a new seasonal "camp" building class at a lower per-square-foot rate and backed a higher new growth estimate.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors met in person with early Zoom trouble. It heard Vision Government Solutions explain the FY24 revaluation process and Nate Kramer of MFS report on his work. It signed invoices and abatements, voted a seasonal cottage classification and supported a raised new growth estimate for town meeting, then entered executive session.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted to create a seasonal cottage classification, coded as camp, at a per-square-foot rate set below the current bungalow rate.
The board voted to support a raised new growth estimate for town meeting.
Vision Government Solutions briefed the board on the FY24 revaluation and asked it to pick a target ratio between 90 and 100 percent of market value.
The board voted to relieve a sewer betterment commitment after a payment and approved a run of invoices, including the principal assessor job advertisement.
Senior exemption questions and citizen questions ended without resolution; the board then entered executive session.

why_it_matters: The camp classification sets how seasonal cottages are assessed, so owners of those buildings (not the land) may see a different assessment than under the bungalow rate.
The new growth estimate that town meeting relies on feeds into how much tax levy the town can raise, which touches the tax bill and the vote residents will be asked to take.
watch_next: The November 20th agenda, where the Q3 tax bill insert is due to return and the board plans to add the executive session minutes for approval and release.
Nate Kramer of MFS is due back in about two weeks for extensive questioning by the board.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main votes (membership, RRC, Vision, MMA advertising, MFS, WB Mason, seasonal cottage rate, new growth) and on the main decisions. They differ on the new growth figure, where ours reads $484,000 and the official minutes read $400,000; on the lack of any recorded vote for the sewer betterment commitment; and on who attended.
